w: I'm considering to buy a car.
r: I'm considering buying a car.
y: After consider, use the -ing form.
a: Enjoy, avoid and finish work the same way!
e: We're considering moving to a new city.
She considered taking a taxi.
q: Consider is followed by the -ing form.
s: Save this before you buy anything.

w: I watched a bird for a second.
r: I saw a bird.
y: See just happens. Look is on purpose.
a: You watch TV, but see a movie!
e: Look at this photo!
We watched the game all night.
m: see = eyes open, look = point, watch = time
q: Did you ___ the football game last night?
A game goes on for a long time, so we watch it.
s: Send this to a confused friend.

w: I forgot my sleep bag.
r: I forgot my sleeping bag.
y: It's a bag for sleeping, so use sleeping.
a: Same with swimming pool and washing machine!
e: Bring a warm sleeping bag for the camping trip.
My sleeping bag is too small.
q: Pack your ___ for the camping trip.
The correct name is sleeping bag.
s: Save this for your next camping trip.

w: I'll buy the real book, not a copy.
r: I'll buy a copy of the book.
y: A copy is often one real book.
a: One copy of a newspaper is real!
e: I bought two copies of the magazine.
Please make a copy of this page.
q: The library has three ___ of this book.
The plural of copy is copies.
s: Save this and share it with a reader.

w: COM-pe-ti-tion
r: com-pe-TI-tion
y: Words ending in -tion: stress the part before -tion.
a: Same with information and education!
e: She won the dance competition.
There is a lot of competition for jobs.
q: Where is the stress in competition?
s: Save this and say it out loud.

w: The hotel is near to the beach.
r: The hotel is near the beach.
y: Near already means close to. No extra to.
a: You can say close to, but just near!
e: We live near the station.
Is there a cafe near here?
s: Save this for your next trip.

w: The report states the prices went up.
r: The report states that prices went up.
y: In formal English, state is often followed by that.
a: State sounds formal. In chat, people just say say!
e: The rules state that phones must be off.
The email states that the meeting is canceled.
q: The letter ___ that the office is closed.
State is followed by that and a fact.
s: Save this for your next report.

w: Please, no disturbing me.
r: Do not disturb.
y: Hotels use this fixed sign. Don't change the words.
a: Many phones have a Do Not Disturb mode too!
e: I put the do not disturb sign on my door.
Turn on do not disturb before the meeting.
q: The sign on the hotel door says: Do not ___.
The fixed phrase is do not disturb.
s: Save this for your next hotel stay.

w: In my opinion, I think it's good.
r: In my opinion, it's good.
y: In my opinion already means I think.
a: It's the same idea twice!
e: In my opinion, the movie was too long.
I think the plan is great.
m: in my opinion = I think (pick ONE)
q: Use one of them, not both.
s: Save this for your next speaking test.

w: I met her three years before.
r: I met her three years ago.
y: Ago counts back from now.
a: Ago always comes after the time: two days ago!
e: He left ten minutes ago.
I had never been there before.
q: I started this job two years ___.
s: Send this to a friend who says before.

w: What is my follow number?
r: What is my tracking number?
y: You track a package with a tracking number.
a: Track means follow the path of something!
e: I got a tracking number by email.
Enter your tracking number on the website.
q: Use the ___ number to check where your package is.
The correct term is tracking number.
s: Save this for your next online order.

w: I'm looking for a work.
r: I'm looking for a job.
y: Job is countable. Work is not.
a: You can say: I'm looking for work!
e: She got a new job at a bank.
I have a lot of work this week.
q: After a, use the countable word job.
s: Save this for your next interview.

w: bi-CY-cle
r: BI-cy-cle
y: The stress is on the first part: BI.
a: Most people just say bike!
e: I ride my bicycle to school.
Her bicycle is red.
q: Where is the stress in bicycle?
s: Save this and say it three times.

w: She smiled to me.
r: She smiled at me.
y: You smile at a person, like you look at them.
a: Laugh works the same way: laugh at!
e: The baby smiled at her mom.
He always smiles at customers.
s: Save this and smile at someone today.

w: Although it rained, but we went out.
r: Although it rained, we went out.
y: Use although or but. Never both.
a: Many languages use two words here. English uses one!
e: Although I was tired, I finished my work.
It was cold, but we went swimming.
q: Although he was sick, ___ he went to work.
s: Save this for your next essay.

w: Sorry for my answering late.
r: Sorry for the late reply.
y: This is the fixed phrase for slow emails.
a: Short and polite. Nobody needs a long excuse!
e: Sorry for the late reply. I was traveling.
Hi Anna, sorry for the late reply.
m: late email? → SORRY FOR THE LATE REPLY
q: The fixed phrase is sorry for the late reply.
s: Save this for your next work email.

w: I like listening music.
r: I like listening to music.
y: Listen needs to before the thing you hear.
a: But you can just say: listen! with no object.
e: We listen to the radio in the car.
Listen to me, please.
q: Listen needs to before an object.
s: Send this to a friend who says it.

w: Every of us came.
r: Each of us came.
y: Each can go before of. Every can't.
a: Every one, as two words, works!
e: Every child needs love.
Each room has its own bathroom.
q: ___ of my friends came to the party.
Only each can go before of.
s: Save this and test a friend.

w: Can I pay with my bank card?
r: Can I pay with my debit card?
y: In the US, people say debit card.
a: Credit card? You pay later!
e: I paid with my debit card.
My debit card is linked to my checking account.
q: A ___ card takes money directly from your bank account.
Debit takes the money right away.
s: Save this for your next shopping trip.

w: It's cold. Turn on the warmer.
r: It's cold. Turn on the heater.
y: A machine that makes heat is a heater.
a: In cars, it's also called the heat: turn on the heat!
e: The heater in my room is broken.
Can you turn off the heater?
q: It's freezing. Can you turn on the ___?
A device that makes heat is a heater.
s: Save this for the cold season.

w: IN-di-vi-du-al
r: in-di-VI-du-al
y: The strong part is VI in the middle.
a: Long words often hide the stress in the middle!
e: Each individual has a vote.
We need help from every individual.
q: Where is the stress in individual?
s: Save this and practice it today.

w: What's the reason of the delay?
r: What's the reason for the delay?
y: We say reason for something.
a: But: the reason why it happened is also fine!
e: There's a good reason for this rule.
What's the reason for your visit?
s: Save this for your next meeting.

w: Take an umbrella if it rains.
r: Take an umbrella in case it rains.
y: In case means: be ready, just to be safe.
a: With in case, you take the umbrella now!
e: Write it down in case you forget.
I'll bring snacks in case we get hungry.
m: IN CASE = just to be safe
q: Save the file ___ the computer crashes.
In case means to be safe before it happens.
s: Save this, just in case!

w: It's depend.
r: It depends.
y: It needs -s: it depends.
a: You can add on: it depends on the weather!
e: Will I go? It depends on my boss.
How long is the trip? It depends.
s: Save this for your next speaking test.

w: I study hard for pass the exam.
r: I study hard to pass the exam.
y: To show why you do something, use to plus verb.
a: For + noun: for the exam!
e: I saved money to buy a bike.
She runs every day to stay healthy.
q: I went to the store ___ milk.
Use to plus a verb for a reason.
s: Save this before your next exam.

w: I have few friends, so I'm happy.
r: I have a few friends, so I'm happy.
y: A few is some. Few is not many.
a: One small word changes the feeling!
e: Few people came, so it was quiet.
I need a few minutes.
m: A few = some 🙂, few = not many 🙁
q: Good news! We have ___ tickets left.
A few means some, which is good news.
s: Send this to a friend who forgets a.

w: I want a two-bed room, please.
r: I'd like a twin room, please.
y: Two single beds in a hotel? That's a twin room.
a: One big bed for two is a double room!
e: We booked a twin room for two nights.
Is the twin room available tonight?
q: Two friends need two beds. They book a ___ room.
A twin room has two single beds.
s: Save this for your next hotel booking.

w: Your phone is very class.
r: Your phone is very classy.
y: Class is a noun. Classy means stylish.
a: Class can also mean groups in society, like the middle class!
e: She comes from a working class family.
That hotel is really classy.
q: Most people in the city are middle ___.
Middle class is a noun phrase.
s: Save this and share it with a friend.

w: Stress can lead for health problems.
r: Stress can lead to health problems.
y: Lead to means cause.
a: Like a road, it leads to the result!
e: Too much sugar can lead to problems.
Hard work led to success.
q: Lead takes to when it means cause.
s: Save this for your next essay.

w: I decided going home.
r: I decided to go home.
y: After decide, use to plus verb.
a: Plan, hope and want also take to!
e: She decided to study abroad.
We decided to stay in.
q: Decide is followed by to plus verb.
s: Save this and decide to practice!

w: Let's divide the bill.
r: Let's split the bill.
y: For sharing a cost, we say split the bill.
a: You can split a taxi too!
e: We always split the bill with friends.
Can we split the bill three ways?
q: Dinner was great. Let's ___ the bill.
Split the bill is the natural phrase.
s: Send this to the friend who never pays.

w: He said me that he was busy.
r: He told me that he was busy.
y: Tell needs a person. Say doesn't.
a: You can say it TO me, but tell ME!
e: She said that she was tired.
Tell me your name.
q: Tell is followed by a person.
s: Send this to a friend who says it.

w: There's an opportunity of rain.
r: There's a chance of rain.
y: Opportunity is a good moment. Chance can mean maybe.
a: Weather news always says chance!
e: This job is a great opportunity.
There's a possibility that he's right.
q: A good moment to do something is an opportunity.
s: Save this for your next speaking test.

w: The smoke finder beeps when I cook.
r: The smoke detector beeps when I cook.
y: A small device that senses smoke is a smoke detector.
a: Detect means find!
e: Check the smoke detector every month.
The smoke detector needs a new battery.
q: The ___ beeps when there is smoke.
The device is called a smoke detector.
s: Save this and check your detector today.

w: One-way ticket to Boston and back, please.
r: A round-trip ticket to Boston, please.
y: One-way means you go but don't come back.
a: One-way street means cars go in one direction only!
e: I bought a one-way ticket to Paris.
Is this a one-way street?
q: You're not coming back. You need a ___ ticket.
s: Save this for your next trip.

w: The gym is available for all students.
r: The gym is available to all students.
y: For people who can use it, say available to.
a: But: I'm available for a meeting at 3!
e: The service is available to members.
This app is available to everyone.
m: available TO people, FOR a time
q: Free Wi-Fi is available ___ all guests.
Use available to with the people who can use it.
s: Save this for your next work email.

w: I suppose to be at work at nine.
r: I'm supposed to be at work at nine.
y: Be supposed to means it's the rule or plan.
a: Fast speech: supposta!
e: You're supposed to wear a helmet.
The train was supposed to leave at six.
q: Use be supposed to for a plan or rule.
s: Save this and say it right tomorrow.

w: Please make tidy your room.
r: Please tidy up your room.
y: Tidy up means put things back in their place.
a: Clean up uses water. Tidy up doesn't!
e: Let's tidy up the kitchen after dinner.
I tidied up my desk.
m: TIDY UP = everything in its place
q: Guests are coming! Let's ___ the living room.
Tidy up is the natural phrase.
s: Send this to someone with a messy room.

w: It has a big effect to the economy.
r: It has a big effect on the economy.
y: Effect, impact and influence all take on.
a: Three words, one rule. Easy points in writing!
e: Music has a calming effect on me.
Phones have an impact on sleep.
q: Sleep has a big effect ___ your mood.
s: Save this for your next essay.

w: Please rise your hand.
r: Please raise your hand.
y: Raise moves something. Rise moves by itself.
a: The sun rises. Nobody raises it!
e: Prices rise every year.
Raise your glass!
q: The sun goes up by itself, so it rises.
s: Save this and test a friend.

w: I need to get a flu injection.
r: I need to get a flu shot.
y: In everyday American English, it's a flu shot.
a: A shot is any injection in casual talk!
e: I got my flu shot at the pharmacy.
Flu shots are free here.
q: Many people get a flu ___ every fall.
The common word is flu shot.
s: Save this for your next doctor visit.

w: I eat diet to lose weight.
r: I'm on a diet to lose weight.
y: On a diet means eating less.
a: Everyone has a diet, even pizza lovers!
e: A healthy diet has lots of vegetables.
She's on a diet this month.
m: diet = your food, ON a diet = eating less
q: I want to lose weight, so I'm ___ a diet.
s: Save this before your next diet.

w: time-TA-ble
r: TIME-ta-ble
y: Stress the first part: TIME.
a: Americans often say schedule instead!
e: Check the bus timetable.
The new timetable starts on Monday.
q: Where is the stress in timetable?
s: Save this for your next train trip.

w: This room is not fit to a party.
r: This room is not fit for a party.
y: Fit for means good enough for.
a: Fit for a king means very, very good!
e: Is he fit for work today?
This food is not fit for children.
q: This old car isn't fit ___ long trips.
Fit for means good enough for.
s: Save this and share it with a friend.

w: If I will be rich, I would travel.
r: If I were rich, I would travel.
y: For dreams, use if plus past, then would.
a: If I were you is perfect, even with I!
e: If I had time, I would help.
If she knew, she would call.
q: If I ___ a car, I would drive to work.
Use the past after if for dreams.
s: Save this and use it today.

w: What time do I leave the hotel?
r: What time do I check out?
y: Check out means pay and leave a hotel.
a: Check out also means look at!
e: We check out at 11 a.m.
Can I check out late?
m: check IN = arrive, check OUT = leave
q: Check out means leave the hotel.
s: Save this for your next hotel stay.

w: A solution for this problem is easy.
r: A solution to this problem is easy.
y: The usual form is solution to a problem.
a: Answer works the same: answer to!
e: We found a solution to the problem.
Is there a solution to traffic?
q: The answer ___ this question is simple.
s: Save this for your next essay.

w: My hourly salary is fifteen dollars.
r: My hourly wage is fifteen dollars.
y: Pay by the hour is a wage. A salary is yearly.
a: Minimum wage is always wage, never salary!
e: Her salary is paid every month.
Waiters often earn a low wage.
q: He earns twenty dollars an hour. That's his ___.
Pay per hour is a wage.
s: Save this for your next interview.
